content:
Just by looking at some of the comments here, you'll find a group of people vocally opposing all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. As a result, an unofficial tool has emerged that lets users disable this feature on Mac and delete all downloaded Siri AI models.

We warned yesterday that this approach could carry risks, but now some believe Apple may need to officially support the ability to remove AI features in order to protect hardware sales…

In recent years, opposition to generative AI has continued to grow, with critics citing a wide range of reasons—from fears about the survival of the human species to simply not wanting unwanted AI features taking up storage space on their devices.

The latest Apple Intelligence models require up to 14GB of storage space. If you don't want these features, the impact is quite significant on a 256GB device. Independent developer Om Lahore has therefore created a project called RemoveMacAI.

Ewolf's popular comment

I've turned off AI and SIRI on all browsers on both my computer and phone. I'm enjoying a web experience roughly like 2012 again—it's absolutely wonderful.

I don't need it, don't want it, and won't miss AI.

We warned yesterday that using this tool is not without risk. Since Apple Intelligence is deeply embedded in macOS 27, it may cause unwanted side effects on some basic functions.

But some believe Apple should provide an official way for users to remove Apple Intelligence on Mac. John Gruber of Daring Fireball has pointed out that some organisations have already banned the installation of AI tools.

To be clear, Apple does offer quite a few management options for organisations using device management. Apple currently states that organisations can "restrict the use" of certain Apple Intelligence features, and there are individual toggles to enable or disable specific features one by one. What's currently missing is a master switch to disable all Apple Intelligence features at once, along with an option to remove downloaded models.

This issue isn't urgent for now, but as future Mac models gradually drop support for older versions of macOS, if Apple continues to make it difficult to remove AI models, it may start to affect hardware sales.
